narrationScript: Now we arrive at a critical safety lesson for both UPDATE and DELETE statements. We've seen how the WHERE clause acts as a filter, ensuring your commands only affect the specific rows you intend. But what happens if you forget it? This is where extreme caution is needed. If you omit the WHERE clause in an UPDATE statement, the database will attempt to update *every single row* in the table. Imagine changing every student's major to 'Data Science' by accident! Similarly, if you run a DELETE statement without a WHERE clause, *all rows* will be removed from your table. This is equivalent to emptying the entire table, and in many systems, it's an irreversible operation outside of a transaction. To prevent such catastrophic data loss, a wise precaution is to first run a SELECT query with the *exact same* WHERE clause you plan to use for your UPDATE or DELETE. This allows you to verify *which* rows would be affected *before* you make any permanent changes. Always, always, double-check your WHERE clause.
